trajectory.patch:
Based on the Kconfig warning, `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` is being set in configurations where its dependency `CONFIG_USERSPACE` is not enabled. This happens because this test suite is likely executed in both userspace and non-userspace configurations, but the project configuration files unconditionally set `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`.

The fix involves two parts:
1.  A latent bug in `src/main.c` is fixed where a call to `k_thread_access_grant()` was missing its required `NULL` terminator. This bug could lead to undefined behavior and may have been the original reason for increasing `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES`. With this bug fixed, the number of granted objects is definitively 3.
2.  `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES=6` is removed from all project configuration files (`prj.conf`, `prj_multiq.conf`, `prj_simple.conf`). After fixing the bug above, the default value for `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` (which is 4) is sufficient for the userspace tests. Removing this configuration item resolves the Kconfig warning for non-userspace builds without affecting userspace builds.

Here are the precise changes:

tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/prj.conf
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES=6
CONFIG_TEST_USERSPACE=y
========
CONFIG_TEST_USERSPACE=y
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/prj_multiq.conf
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES=6
CONFIG_MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=1
========
CONFIG_MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=1
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/prj_simple.conf
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES=6
CONFIG_MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=1
========
CONFIG_MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS=1
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/src/main.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
	k_thread_access_grant(k_current_get(), &user_thread, &user_sem,
			      &ustack);
========
	k_thread_access_grant(k_current_get(), &user_thread, &user_sem,
			      &ustack, NULL);
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
